DWG 01ATITLE IMPACT SO FARREV 29 OCT 2026STATUS VALIDATED BY L&T

What Changed for L&T

Effort is only worth counting when it moves something. These are the outcomes L&T itself has confirmed in writing or in session, and what each one means for how PES projects will run.

OUTCOME 1 · 5 OCT 2026

The Drawing Engine Works on L&T’s Own Drawings

L&T’s AI Centre of Excellence ran the proof of concept itself, inside its network, and confirmed that BOM tables and revision tables were extracted successfully. Item and variation tables were extracted by the Applutions engine.

What it meansThe 9/10 challenge of re-keying drawing data into PLM and ERP by hand now has a proven, on-premise answer. The remaining step is secure access to Seclore-protected files, which L&T is resolving through a Seclore API.
OUTCOME 2 · 5 OCT 2026

The Dashboard Prototype Is L&T’s Baseline

L&T confirmed the working prototype as “a good baseline and conceptual prototype” for the Unified Operational Visibility Dashboard and is now evaluating vendors and a platform to build it end to end.

What it means24+ projects across 6 domains will be visible in one place, with escalations and dependencies surfaced before weekly reviews. L&T owns production; Applutions supports the AI and insights layer.
OUTCOME 3 · 5 OCT 2026

Post-Delivery Revisions Move to Build

L&T found the Delivered-System Revision Register architecture suitable and is routing it to its IT & Digital team as a system-integration build, with Applutions scoping the data sources, interfaces and data elements.

What it meansFor the first time, a revision raised after dispatch can be traced to every delivered system built to the earlier version, instead of relying on recall.
OUTCOME 4 · MAR TO OCT 2026

From a Wide List to 4 Funded Priorities

131 pages of as-is understanding and 26 rated challenges let L&T choose with evidence: BOM alignment, drawing revisions, execution visibility and post-delivery revisions, now 4 solutions progressing in parallel.

What it meansEvery AI investment is tied to a mapped, rated problem and an agreed owner, and the same as-is study is the reference for every team that joins.
4 of 4Table types extracted from drawings
6Domains unified in the accepted dashboard baseline
84Defence companies profiled, 5 shortlisted for outreach
36 + 177Indian institutions mapped, with official contacts
Design rules that heldEverything L&T accepted runs inside its own network on Infor ERP LN, PLM, Concerto, SQMS and SAHACHAR data; AI suggests and people confirm; every number is calculated, never guessed; and the integration layer is built to add SAP later without rework.

One Map of How a Project Really Runs

Before suggesting any AI, we wrote down how work actually flows today: who owns what, which system holds which data, and where people step in by hand. It grew from 91 pages in June to 131 pages, and it is now the shared reference for every solution.

The Project Lifecycle, Start to Finish

RFQEnquiry
Pre-OrderCosting, bid
TransitionProject setup
EngineeringDrawings, BOM
ProcurementPPO, vendors
PlanningSchedules
ExecutionShop floor
MonitoringStatus, risk
AcceptanceFAT · HAT · SAT · TLS

5 Core Systems, Mapped

What each system does and where data has to be copied between them by hand.

PLMDrawings, HBOM, revisions and change workflows
ERP LNOrders, demand, production and inventory (FKMS within ERP)
ConcertoCCPM scheduling, FPR updates and buffers
SQMSInspection calls and QC offering
SAHACHARVendor portal: PO visibility and inspection coordination

Who Owns What

Ownership agreed across 9 functions in the 9 April review.

  • Design is the source of truth for drawings and BOM
  • PMG is the central coordination and scheduling layer
  • Supply chain is the execution arm

How a bill of materials changes shape as it moves through the business:

EBOM→MBOM→PBOM
In plain termsThe engineering BOM lists what the design needs; the manufacturing BOM lists how it will be built; the production BOM lists what the shop floor orders. Gaps open when one changes and the others do not follow.

20 AI Solutions in 8 Transformation Clusters

Every challenge has a designed answer. Each of the 20 solutions has its own architecture document with block diagrams, data flows and an end-to-end table. 4 are in build now, and on 5 October L&T asked for the next level of detail: named data sources, interfaces and data elements so its development teams can implement directly.

5 Rules Every Solution Follows

On-premiseAll data, processing and AI models stay inside L&T’s network.
No outside AI callsOpen-source models run on L&T’s own GPUs.
People decideAI suggests; an engineer or PMG lead confirms.
Exact numbersKPIs are calculated, never guessed by the AI.
Right accessRole-based access and a full audit trail.
Solutions 1 and 2 · Engineering intelligence

EDIE and ERDIE

EDIE reads engineering drawings and turns them into clean, structured data: revision tables, BOM tables, item tables and variation tables. ERDIE then works out what a revision changes downstream, so procurement and production are told before they act on an old drawing.

~12,000Drawing types in scope

2 routesSeclore API decryption, or extraction before protection
Human checkEngineers review before anything is published

Solution 21 · Post-delivery revision control

Delivered-System Revision Register

When a revision is raised after a system has shipped, this solution finds every delivered system built to the earlier version, assembles its as-built record, and routes the right action. Added after L&T raised it in August as the next high-priority problem. On 5 October L&T found the architecture suitable and is routing it to IT & Digital as a system-integration build.

Challenge 8.1ArchitectureReviewed by L&TData sources and interfaces for IT & Digital

Research Into the Technology Base

A 54-page open-source research evaluation (3 September) reviewed 12 projects for the dashboard, scored on licence safety, maturity and fit. It is research input, not the chosen stack: L&T is running its own platform proof of concept and evaluating implementation vendors. One principle carried into the architecture: serve the dashboard from an L&T-owned data store and never query the ERP live, which keeps load and licensing under control.

#ProjectRole in the platformLicence

Access Control and AI Governance

A 16-page blueprint for who can see what: role-based permissions, project-level scope and governed AI. It starts with a narrow, read-only AI pilot that summarises one project’s status and blockers, released only after access checks pass.

ERP today, SAP-readyAll 4 solutions integrate with Infor ERP LN, the ERP in use. ERP access sits behind one adapter and one canonical data model, so an SAP adapter can be added later without re-platforming.
DWG 07TITLE DEFENCE STARTUPSREV 84 COMPANIES · OCT 2026STATUS 5 SHORTLISTED

India’s Defence-Tech Bench, Mapped for L&T

L&T’s Laksha roadmap seeks startups that can grow to ₹1,000 to 2,000 crore of revenue within 5 years. We built an institutional reference of 84 companies across 16 data fields, scored against the capabilities autonomous systems need, and extended it in October with 10 companies chosen for fit with PES: missile subsystems, precision components, RF electronics, naval AI and autonomy.

The 4-Layer Lens

Every startup is placed on the layer of an autonomous system it strengthens. India is strongest today in execution platforms; the future value sits in cognition and coordination.

LAYER 1PerceptionSensing: radar, EO/IR, satellites
LAYER 2CognitionDecision-making: AI, edge compute
LAYER 3ExecutionMovement: drones, UGVs, propulsion
LAYER 4CoordinationSwarms, C4ISR, secure comms

Research Partners in the US and India

Universities can do early-stage research that is hard to fund in-house. We mapped where each institution’s strengths meet L&T’s themes, named the right contacts, and designed a model that keeps L&T’s intellectual property safe.

13 Global Institutions

12 named contacts and 5 meetings held by mid-June. Each line says how the partnership helps L&T.

    36 Indian Institutions

    In September L&T chose to focus on Indian universities: on 23 September Mr Sameer Raikar confirmed interest in Indian collaborations and asked for the institutions with a common area of interest. By 11 October we delivered a tracker of 36 institutions with capability maps, funding and defence links, and a directory of 177 official contacts; the common-interest shortlist is the next deliverable.

    An IP-Safe Way to Collaborate

    Early research (Technology Readiness Levels 2 to 5) is done with university partners; later development and commercialisation stay with L&T in India, with export-control rules respected throughout.
